thread:
jess: Quick flag  noticed a routing variance after the recent header consolidation. Some tenants seeing higher latency and token cost. Suspect mismatch between `x-rd-route` and `x-rd-route-id`.
omar: Confirmed. The new router expects `x-rd-route-id`. Older SDKs (notably pinned Go clients) still emit `x-rd-route`.
lina: Effects: 1) requests without `x-rd-route-id` land on fallback path with lower throughput; 2) console shows these tenants under 'unrouted' causing confusing billing spikes.
ben: Can we make the router accept both names for a short window? A shim in the ingress layer mapping `x-rd-route` -> `x-rd-route-id` should be safe.
jess: That'd mitigate immediate customer impact. We also need SDK work: patch TS/Python to include a runtime compat mode that emits both headers when enabled.
omar: I'll open a small PR to add the shim and gate it behind `compat.route_headers=true`. Will include unit tests and a metric `compat.route_headers.active`.
lina: Console side: add a temporal annotation on the tenant dashboards and mute the high-cost alert for affected tenants while we backfill. I'll coordinate with observability.
ben: SDK plan: TS/py dual-header opt-in for one release. For Go, offer a patch release and reach out to customers who pin older versions. Also add e2e test asserting routing when only old header present.
ci-bot: deploy queued  ingress/route-shim v0.9.1 -> canary (us-east-1)
jess: Action items: omar deploy shim & flag (canary today), lina to annotate dashboards + mute alerts, ben to cut SDK patches and open a support playbook, and we'll draft a short migration note in devex.
omar: PR created: github.com/redwood/route-negotiator/pull/918. Adding rollback switch.
ben: SDK patches scheduled for today. Will make dual-header behind `enable_route_compat` config and note WAF caveat in release notes.
jess: Good. After canary looks green we'll flip the flag for 48h and run a targeted backfill of routing metrics for affected tenants. Follow-up in #postmortems to finalize deprecation timeline.
